name: Sahifa
tagline: A coffee shop where people read

listing.description: A site for a book café, literary club or small bookshop. A shelf of spines on the first screen, books of the month in classic cover style and club meetings as cards.

seo.title: Sahifa — coffee shop and book club in Tashkent
seo.description: Coffee, pastries and a thousand books on the shelves at 31 Buyuk Ipak Yuli St. A book club on Wednesdays, a book swap and quiet reading tables. Open 9 am to 11 pm.
seo.answer: Sahifa is a coffee shop with a library at 31 Buyuk Ipak Yuli St in Tashkent, open daily from 9 am to 11 pm. A cappuccino costs 26,000 UZS; the Wednesday book club at 7 pm is 60,000 UZS with coffee and dessert. Books on the shelves are free to read and swap.

business.street: 31 Buyuk Ipak Yuli St, Mirzo Ulugbek

sections.title: A cup of coffee and one more chapter
sections.subtitle: A thousand books on the shelves to read at your table, fresh pastries and coffee from the roaster next door. Book club on Wednesdays, book swap on Sundays.

sections.label: About
sections.title: A library where you can whisper
sections.text: Sahifa means “page” in Uzbek. Our books came from the home libraries of friends and readers: classics, contemporary fiction, books in three languages. Take any of them to your table, and leave one of yours on the swap shelf. There are sockets, but please take loud calls out to the terrace.

items.a: Not from the main shelves — read at your table. From the swap shelf, yes, if you leave one of yours.

items.q: How do I join the book club?
items.a: Leave a request and we send you the book of the week plus a reminder. It costs 60,000 UZS with coffee and dessert.

items.q: Can I work on a laptop?
items.a: Yes, in the window room. Calls go to the terrace so readers aren’t disturbed.
Yes, about a third of the shelves are Uzbek literature and translations into Uzbek.
